page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6.6xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 24 dedicated vCPUs driven by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. It features 192.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB of RAM allocated per virtual core. The platform integrates a baseline network throughput of 8 Gbps and operates without dedicated hardware accelerators or GPUs.

Storage architecture on the instance relies entirely on remote networked volumes, as no local disk storage is bundled. System provisioning requires network-attached cloud disks for all operating system and persistent data needs. The absence of local solid-state drives prevents ephemeral storage IOPS contention, though disk throughput remains dependent on network storage parameters.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the resource ratio delivers high memory capacity per compute unit, reducing operational expenses for applications bounded primarily by memory footprints rather than raw compute cycles. Architectural tradeoffs include the reliance on external storage arrays for high-throughput I/O and standard 8 Gbps networking capabilities. The configuration is suited for in-memory caching systems, distributed memory caches, enterprise transactional databases, and large-scale data processing workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6.6xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server based on the x86_64 architecture and KVM hypervisor. It is equipped with 24 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz and provides 192.0 GB of RAM, yielding an allocation of 8.0 GB of memory per core. The instance includes an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile, with no integrated GPUs or local disks bundled with the hardware. Because persistent storage must be mounted via external network-attached volumes, storage performance relies on remote storage configurations. The 1:8 compute-to-RAM ratio delivers efficient resource scaling for workloads constrained by memory rather than processing throughput. This instance configuration is suitable for large in-memory databases, key-value stores, distributed analytics platforms, and enterprise data processing environments requiring reliable memory capacity.
